provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: BECE phe marathon
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list skills required for marathon running, explain health benefits of marathon, and solve past BECE questions on marathon.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about marathon running in Physical Education. We have studied different athletic events before and now we focus on marathon for BECE.

Content:
Marathon is a long-distance race of 42.195 kilometers. Marathon skills include pacing, endurance, and proper breathing. Health benefits are improved heart health, weight management, and stress reduction. Past BECE questions often ask about training methods and safety precautions. Nigerian examples include the Lagos City Marathon and Abuja International Marathon.

Class activity:
Students will run a mini-marathon of 2km around the school field while practicing proper pacing and breathing techniques.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the standard distance of a marathon?
2. List two health benefits of marathon running.
3. Explain how proper breathing helps in marathon.
4. How would you prepare a student for their first marathon?

Summary:
Marathon requires specific skills and offers many health benefits that are important for BECE examination.

topics.title: Mock examination
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to complete a full mock BECE paper, mark their own papers using the marking guide, and identify areas needing improvement.

Introduction:
We have practiced different topics in Physical Education throughout the term. Today we will take a full mock examination to prepare for BECE.

Content:
Mock examinations help students get familiar with the BECE format and time management. The paper will cover all topics in our scheme of work. Students must work independently and within the time limit. After completion, we will use the marking guide to score papers. Common mistakes include poor time allocation and unreadable handwriting. Nigerian examples include using past questions from states like Lagos and Anambra.

Class activity:
Students will write a complete mock BECE Physical Education paper under exam conditions, then exchange papers for marking using the provided guide.

Evaluation questions:
1. Why are mock examinations important?
2. What are three common mistakes in mock exams?
3. How did you manage your time during the mock?
4. Which topic was most difficult for you in the mock?

Summary:
Mock exams help students identify strengths and weaknesses before the real BECE examination.

topics.title: Practical exam prep
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate their best practical skills, explain the techniques used, and create a practice plan to improve.

Introduction:
We have learned many practical skills in Physical Education. Today we will focus on our best skills to prepare for the practical examination.

Content:
Practical exams test physical skills like throwing, jumping, and running. Students should identify their strongest events and perfect them. Techniques include proper form, follow-through, and body positioning. Practice should be regular with specific goals. Nigerian examples include practicing with local equipment like sand for long jump and homemade targets for throwing.

Class activity:
Each student will demonstrate their best practical skill while others observe and provide constructive feedback.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is your strongest practical skill in PHE?
2. Explain the proper technique for your chosen skill.
3. How often should you practice before the exam?
4. What equipment do you need for your skill?

Summary:
Focusing on strengths and regular practice will help students perform well in practical exams.

topics.title: Inter house sports
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to participate in inter-house sports events, demonstrate good sportsmanship, and record house performance results.

Introduction:
We have learned about sports competitions and teamwork. Today we will participate in inter-house sports to demonstrate these skills.

Content:
Inter-house sports involve competition between different school houses. Events include track and field, ball games, and traditional sports. Students must show respect for opponents and officials. Records are kept of individual and team performances. Nigerian examples include the annual inter-house sports day with events like sack race and tug of war.

Class activity:
Students will participate in various inter-house sports events including relay races, football matches, and traditional Nigerian games.

Evaluation questions:
1. Why is sportsmanship important in inter-house sports?
2. Name two events commonly found in inter-house sports.
3. How do records help in sports competitions?
4. What makes inter-house sports enjoyable for students?

Summary:
Inter-house sports promote teamwork, physical fitness, and healthy competition among students.

topics.title: Weakness clinics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify their weak topics in PHE, create targeted drills to improve, and demonstrate improvement through practice.

Introduction:
We have practiced many topics in Physical Education. Today we will focus on areas where we need improvement to strengthen our performance.

Content:
Identifying weaknesses is crucial for exam success. Students should analyze past tests and mock exams to find problem areas. Targeted drills focus on specific skills with repetition and feedback. Common weaknesses include theory concepts and practical techniques. Nigerian examples include practicing with local equipment like stones for shot put and measuring distances with traditional methods.

Class activity:
Students will form small groups based on shared weaknesses and create specific drills to practice together.

Evaluation questions:
1. How can you identify your weak topics in PHE?
2. Why are targeted drills more effective than general practice?
3. Give an example of a drill for improving throwing accuracy.
4. How will you know if your weakness clinic is working?

Summary:
Focused practice on weaknesses helps students overcome challenges and improve overall performance.

topics.title: Health project
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to design a health campaign, create educational materials, and present their campaign to the class.

Introduction:
We have studied various health topics in Physical Education. Today we will create health campaigns to educate others about important health issues.

Content:
Health projects involve researching health topics and creating awareness campaigns. Students should choose relevant issues like nutrition, hygiene, or exercise. Campaign materials include posters, flyers, and presentations. Presentations should be clear, concise, and engaging. Nigerian examples include campaigns about clean water, malaria prevention, or balanced diets using local foods.

Class activity:
Students will create posters and short presentations about health issues affecting Nigerian youth, then present to the class.

Evaluation questions:
1. What makes an effective health campaign?
2. Name three health issues common among Nigerian youth.
3. How can you make your health campaign more engaging?
4. What resources do you need for your health project?

Summary:
Health projects help students develop research skills while promoting important health awareness in their community.

topics.title: Speed and accuracy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to complete timed tests, improve their scores through practice, and apply techniques for better performance.

Introduction:
In Physical Education, both speed and accuracy are important for performance. Today we will practice improving these skills through timed activities.

Content:
Speed and accuracy are crucial in many PHE activities and exam questions. Timed tests help students work quickly without sacrificing quality. Techniques include proper time management, focusing on key points, and eliminating wrong answers. Regular practice builds confidence and reduces exam anxiety. Nigerian examples include practice with local timing devices like gourds for water relay races.

Class activity:
Students will complete timed mini-tests on PHE topics, with each round focusing on improving speed while maintaining accuracy.

Evaluation questions:
1. Why is time management important in PHE exams?
2. How can you improve both speed and accuracy?
3. What techniques help you work faster under pressure?
4. How has your practice improved your test scores?

Summary:
Regular timed practice helps students develop the speed and accuracy needed for successful exam performance.

topics.title: Officiating basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the rules of common games, demonstrate proper officiating signals, and referee a simple game fairly.

Introduction:
We have participated in many sports games. Today we will learn how to officiate these games, which is an important skill for PHE exams.

Content:
Officiating involves enforcing rules, making decisions, and managing games. Officials must know the rules thoroughly and remain neutral. Common signals include hand gestures for fouls, out of bounds, and scores. Good communication with players is essential. Nigerian examples include officiating local games like Ayo and traditional wrestling matches.

Class activity:
Students will take turns refereeing a simple game of football or volleyball while others play, practicing proper signals and fair decisions.

Evaluation questions:
1. What qualities make a good sports official?
2. Name three common officiating signals and their meanings.
3. How should officials communicate with players during a game?
4. Why is neutrality important for officials?

Summary:
Learning to officiate helps students understand sports rules better and develop leadership skills.

topics.title: Final mock
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to complete a full BECE dress rehearsal, apply exam strategies, and review their performance for final preparation.

Introduction:
We have practiced throughout the term with mock exams and practical sessions. Today we will do our final mock to ensure we are fully prepared for BECE.

Content:
The final mock simulates actual BECE conditions exactly. Students must follow all exam rules and time limits. Strategies include reading instructions carefully, managing time per section, and checking answers. After completion, we will review common mistakes and final preparation tips. Nigerian examples include using past questions from previous BECE exams across different states.

Class activity:
Students will write a complete BECE Physical Education paper under strict exam conditions, followed by a group review session.

Evaluation questions:
1. What exam strategies did you use in the final mock?
2. How did the final mock differ from earlier ones?
3. What final preparation will you do before BECE?
4. How confident do you feel about the real exam now?

Summary:
The final mock helps students build confidence and identify any last-minute areas needing attention before BECE.

topics.title: BECE readiness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list exam day tips, prepare necessary materials, and demonstrate proper exam conduct.

Introduction:
Our BECE examination is approaching. Today we will finalize our preparation and ensure we are ready for exam day success.

Content:
Exam day preparation includes having all necessary materials like pencil, eraser, and ruler. Students should arrive early, read instructions carefully, and manage time wisely. Proper exam conduct includes no cheating and following invigilator instructions. Final review should focus on key points rather than new topics. Nigerian examples include bringing water in transparent bottles and wearing proper school uniform as per exam regulations.

Class activity:
Students will pack their exam bags with all necessary materials and practice entering the examination hall quietly and taking their seats properly.

Evaluation questions:
1. What materials are essential for BECE PHE exam?
2. How should you manage your time during the exam?
3. What are three rules of proper exam conduct?
4. How will you handle difficult questions during the exam?

Summary:
Proper preparation and conduct on exam day are crucial for success in BECE Physical Education.
